title: Surgeon cautions against ‘blindly’ using AI for organ allocation
key_facts: Healthcare Brew interviewed Henry Randall, president of the American Society of Transplant Surgeons and a member of the advisory board of Valiant AI, a company developing AI to help decide which patients get donor organs.

Randall said AI 'is not meant to be a standalone working product or service or tool that you can 100% rely on' and that using it blindly, as many are now doing, is not the way to approach it; it needs engineers, data scientists and rigorous statistics around it.
To his knowledge no healthcare system is using AI to predict outcomes and allocate organs beyond research.
CBS News found about 12,000 donated organs were discarded in the US in 2024.
A May 2026 American Heart Association scientific statement found inherent biases in heart allocation along socioeconomic and racial lines.
Randall says the donor population is shifting to people in their 50s and 60s while allocation methods have not changed to match.
quote_evidence: To Randall’s knowledge, no healthcare system is using AI to predict outcomes and allocate organs beyond research.
Henry Randall is on the advisory board of one of those companies, Valiant AI.
Some companies and universities are now developing AI tools to provide support to doctors deciding which patients should get which donor organ.
why_it_matters_hint: AI is being built for organ matching, and a transplant leader warns against using it before people understand it.
